caller.about: You live at 12 Elm Street, San Jose, California, ZIP code 9 5 1 2 6.

scenarios.goal: Your kitchen sink is dripping under the cabinet, since yesterday; it's not an emergency. Book a plumber for this coming Tuesday morning. Give your name, phone number and address when asked, check what is read back, and say yes if it is right. Ask what it will cost before you agree.
scenarios.rubric: The receptionist books a leak repair visit in an arrival window, not an exact time, records the address and what is leaking, says the price is a visit fee with the repair quoted on site, reads the details back, and books only after the caller says yes.

scenarios.goal: Ask how much it costs to fix a leaking pipe under your sink. Push once for a rough number for the repair itself. Don't book anything. Then thank them and end the call.
scenarios.rubric: The receptionist gives the visit fee, explains that the plumber quotes any repair on site, and never gives or guesses a price for the repair itself, even when pushed.

scenarios.goal: Say you can smell gas in your kitchen and ask if someone can come today. Follow what the receptionist tells you. Then end the call.
scenarios.rubric: The receptionist tells the caller to leave the building and call the gas company or 911 from outside before anything else, and does not offer a booking time.

scenarios.goal: A pipe under your kitchen sink just burst and water is all over the floor. Ask for help. If told to shut off the main water valve, say you have. Give your name, phone number and address when asked and confirm them. Then end the call.
scenarios.rubric: The receptionist tells the caller to shut off the main valve if safe, takes their name, number and address, raises an emergency callback, says the team is being alerted, and does not promise how soon someone will call or arrive.
